subject: SLA exception request — customer-managed edge responsibility split
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nightwatch.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: carveout language for customer-controlled edge

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Nightwatch's infra team has one outstanding ask before legal will sign: because we manage the edge peering and an L4 load-balancer in our VPC, sporadic bursts of ~200-400ms tail latency are caused by our router flap and regional peering churn. Our security and procurement teams would like an explicit SLA split so those tail events do not count toward Redwood's latency SLO or uptime credits.

Practically, we're asking for:
- An appendix that excludes customer-managed edge events (defined as incidents where our BGP advertisements or peering state changes) from Redwood uptime calculations.
- A mechanism for Nightwatch to provide authoritative evidence (BGP logs, Peering Manager export) for disputed incidents.
- A fallback eligibility clause that keeps the app online by allowing Redwood to route to a hosted fallback model if the private deployment is unavailable for >10 minutes.

I've attached our simplified network diagram and a proposed mutual action plan. Can you route this to your legal/ops?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of Infrastructure, Nightwatch AI

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nightwatch.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: carveout language for customer-controlled edge

Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Looping in Vanessa (Partner Ops) and Karthik (SRE Legal/Policy) to weigh in. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

- We typically accept evidence-based attribution for network tails, but legal needs a reproducible evidence checklist (what logs, what timestamps).
- The hosted fallback option is feasible, but we need to define routing policy, cost implications, and how model version parity is handled during fallback.
- Can you confirm the expected frequency of these events and an example BGP dump timeframe (one incident) so SRE can triage?

I'll set up a short call with Vanessa and Karthik today.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nightwatch.ai>
Date: 2028-09-01T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: carveout language for customer-controlled edge

Thanks for the ping. Two operational points before legal drafts:

1) Evidence package: we will accept the following from Nightwatch for attribution review:
   - BGP RIB snapshots for the affected prefix range (UTC timestamps)
   - Router syslogs around the event window (10 min before / 20 min after)
   - Traceroutes from two Redwood probe locations to the affected prefix at 1-min intervals for the incident window
   - A signed statement from Nightwatch NetOps on the time-range and root cause

2) Fallback: If we enable hosted fallback, we need to set:
   - A cooldown period (suggest 10 minutes) before fallback triggers automatically
   - A cost-rate for inference during fallback (per-token uplift)
   - A runbook for state sync if customers use local KV caches (we can provide KV invalidation hooks)

I can draft an ops appendix that enumerates the evidence format and the routing/playback behavior for fallback. Karthik — any legal constraints on explicit carveouts given our SLAs?

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nightwatch.ai>
Date: 2028-09-02T08:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: carveout language for customer-controlled edge

On Fri, Sep 1, 2028 at 15:20 Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> I can draft an ops appendix that enumerates the evidence format and the routing/playback behavior for fallback. Karthik — any legal constraints on explicit carveouts given our SLAs?

Quick take: carveouts are OK if narrowly defined and evidence-based. A few legal guardrails we will include: 
- Carveout triggers must be objective and auditable (timestamps, log artifacts).
- Redwood retains the right to perform independent validation; disputed incidents go to a 3rd-party arbiter after two internal reviews.
- Carveouts cannot be used to avoid remediation obligations when the failure is due to our runtime or a misconfiguration on the private deployment that Redwood manages.

I'll propose language that: (a) defines "Customer-Controlled Edge" explicitly, (b) sets the evidence checklist Vanessa outlined, and (c) adds an escalation path and arbitration clause.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, SRE Policy & Legal Interface, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nightwatch.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-05T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: carveout language for customer-controlled edge

Hi team,

Appreciate the quick alignment. Nightwatch can conform to the evidence checklist — attaching a sample BGP RIB export and a short traceroute log from last week (see attached). A couple of clarifications from our legal counsel: 

- We request a maximum 72-hour window for Redwood to review attribution evidence before any uptime credit is withheld.
- For fallback: we prefer that the default model parity be maintained (same model family/weights) and that any per-token uplift be capped at 1.5x the hosted rate for the first 24 hours of fallback.

If those points look reasonable, let's get a redline of the appendix and the MAP and push to legal. Happy to join a call if helpful.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of Infrastructure, Nightwatch AI
